verdict: 1st Phorm Level-1 is a decent everyday whey and milk protein blend if you like the brand's flavor range, but it isn't cheap for what's on the label. It scores 58 on our Label Score, rank 40 of 100.

verdict: NOW Sports Whey Protein Isolate is a good buy if you want an unflavored, unsweetened whey isolate with almost nothing added. It scores 87 on our Label Score, ranks fourth overall and is the top whey on our list.

A 28 g scoop gives 24 g of protein, about 86 percent of the scoop, at 110 calories, or about 4.6 calories per gram of protein. You get 1 g of carbs, 0 g of sugar and fat, and 45 mg of sodium. There are no sweeteners or flagged additives. The typical amino profile lists 2.5 g of leucine and 5.1 g of BCAAs. Informed Sport, kosher and halal appear on the retailer listing, so they are per NOW; NOW is on the Informed Sport brand list, but we could not confirm this product in the registry. At the dated price on file, $120.28 for 5 lb at Vitacost, it costs about $1.55 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is price per gram compared with a mainstream blend. Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey costs about $1.44 per 25 g and has a registry-verified NSF Certified for Sport listing, but it adds acesulfame potassium and soy lecithin and gives less protein per scoop. Some NOW copy says 25 g of protein; the panel says 24 g.
now-sports-whey-isolate.bestFor: Lifters who want a plain whey isolate with no sweeteners
now-sports-whey-isolate.skipIf: You want the lowest price per gram or a registry-verified certification

verdict: Nutricost Casein is one of the cheapest ways to buy micellar casein, and it's worth it if you want casein on a budget. It scores 63 on our Label Score, rank 31 of 100. Pick something else if you need a certified tub.

The Chocolate panel lists 25 g of protein in a 35 g scoop, so 71% of the scoop is protein, at 120 calories, or 4.8 calories per gram of protein. It has 3 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar (added), 1 g of fiber and 190 mg of sodium. The ingredients are micellar casein with sunflower lecithin, cocoa, natural and artificial flavors, salt and sucralose. Sucralose is the only sweetener, and no gums or flagged additives are listed. There is no named certification, and it is not on the NSF list. The brand page also carries a California Prop 65 warning for lead. At the dated price on file ($82.97 for 64 servings, checked 2026-11-19), it costs $1.30 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is certification. BulkSupplements Casein Protein, with NSF Certified for Sport confirmed in the registry, scores 88 at $1.27 per 25 g, so you get a verified certification for about the same price. One more caution: Nutricost's own product copy says 24 g of protein while the panel says 25 g.
nutricost-casein-protein.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a sucralose-only chocolate casein
nutricost-casein-protein.skipIf: You need a registry-verified certification or avoid sucralose

verdict: Nutricost Whey Protein Concentrate is a fair buy if you want a plain, unsweetened whey in a big tub, but the label leaves gaps. It scores 66 on our Label Score and ranks 23rd overall.

The ingredient list is instantized whey protein concentrate with sunflower lecithin. A 33 g scoop gives 25 g of protein, about 76 percent of the scoop, at 120 calories, or 4.8 calories per gram of protein, with 1 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar, 2 g of fat and 65 mg of sodium. There are no sweeteners or flagged additives. No amino acid profile is shown. Nutricost says it is third-party tested, but no certification is recorded: the product is not in the NSF Certified for Sport registry. At the dated price on file, $109.95 for 5 lb at Vitacost, it costs about $1.59 per 25 g of protein across about 69 servings.

The trade-off is the thin label data. A Target listing shows a different panel, with 73 servings and 130 calories, so check the panel on your tub. Naked Whey offers a similar plain concentrate with a published amino profile and an NSF Contents badge per Naked Nutrition, but costs more, about $1.84 per 25 g.
nutricost-whey-concentrate.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a plain whey concentrate in a 5 lb tub
nutricost-whey-concentrate.skipIf: You need a certified product or a published amino profile

verdict: Oath Clear Protein Powder suits you if you want a juice-style clear whey in fruit flavors rather than a milkshake. As a protein source it is middling, with a lower protein share than other clear wheys and no confirmed certification.

The label maths for Frosty Lemonade: 20 g of protein in a 30 g scoop is 67% protein, and 110 calories works out to 5.5 calories per gram of protein. Carbs are 3 g, sugar 1 g, fat 1 g and sodium 150 mg. Alongside whey protein isolate, the scoop contains coconut milk powder with tapioca maltodextrin, citric and malic acid, and three sweeteners: sucralose, stevia (Reb M) and monk fruit. Milk is inferred from the whey; no Contains line was visible. We found no third-party certification; Oath says it is third-party tested but publishes no results. At the dated price on file ($29.99 for 18 servings at Target, a sale price, checked 2026-11-01) you pay about $2.08 per 25 g. Label Score 50, rank 63 of 100.

The trade-off is protein density. Myprotein Clear Whey Isolate puts protein at 80% of the scoop for about $1.69 per 25 g and scores 76, so it is the stronger clear whey if flavor range is not the deciding factor.
oath-protein-powder.bestFor: Fans of fruity clear whey drinks
oath-protein-powder.skipIf: You avoid sucralose or want the leanest clear whey

verdict: Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Casein is a dependable mainstream casein, but you pay for the brand name. It scores 63 on our Label Score, rank 32 of 100. Buy it if you want a widely sold casein with a familiar label.

The Chocolate Supreme label lists 24 g of protein in a 34 g scoop, so 71% of the scoop is protein, at 120 calories, or 5.0 calories per gram of protein. It has 4 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar, 1 g of fiber and 260 mg of sodium, plus 500 mg of calcium. The ingredients include a gum blend (guar gum, gum acacia, xanthan gum), sunflower and/or soy lecithin, and two sweeteners, acesulfame potassium and sucralose. It contains milk and soy. Informed Choice is per the label and retailer; the registry could not be reached, so we have not confirmed it. At the dated price on file ($86.51 for 53 servings at Vitacost, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $1.70 per 25 g of protein. ON's own site was charging $97.49 for the same size.

The trade-off is additives and cost. Naked Casein, also in our casein family, scores 86 at $1.39 per 25 g. You give up the gums and the second sweetener and save money, though you lose the Gold Standard flavor range.
optimum-nutrition-gold-standard-casein.bestFor: Buyers who want a widely stocked, flavored micellar casein
optimum-nutrition-gold-standard-casein.skipIf: You want fewer gums and sweeteners or a cheaper casein

verdict: Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey is a sensible buy if you want a mainstream flavored whey with a verified sport certification at a fair price. It scores 78 on our Label Score and ranks eighth overall.

Double Rich Chocolate, the flavor on file, uses a blend of whey isolate, concentrate and hydrolyzed whey. A 31 g scoop gives 24 g of protein, about 77 percent of the scoop, at 120 calories, or 5 calories per gram of protein, with 3 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar and 130 mg of sodium. It is sweetened with acesulfame potassium, uses natural and artificial flavor, and contains milk and soy (from lecithin). The brand states 5.5 g of BCAAs but does not publish leucine. NSF Certified for Sport is verified: we confirmed it in the NSF registry for Double Rich Chocolate and Vanilla Ice Cream; other flavors were not listed. At the dated price on file, $79.99 for 3.96 lb at Target, it costs about $1.44 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is the artificial sweetener and a lower protein share than a pure isolate. NOW Sports Whey Protein Isolate gives 24 g of protein in a 28 g scoop with no sweetener, but costs a little more, about $1.55 per 25 g, and its Informed Sport claim is per NOW. Labels vary by lot, so check your tub.
optimum-nutrition-gold-standard-whey.bestFor: Lifters who want a widely sold, NSF-verified flavored whey
optimum-nutrition-gold-standard-whey.skipIf: You avoid artificial sweeteners or soy

verdict: Optimum Nutrition Platinum Hydrowhey is for buyers who specifically want hydrolyzed whey isolate and will pay a premium for it. It scores 59 on our Label Score, rank 39 of 100. For most people, a standard isolate is cheaper and has fewer additives.

The Turbo Chocolate label lists 30 g of protein in a 41 g scoop, so 73% of the scoop is protein, at 140 calories, or 4.7 calories per gram of protein. It has 3 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar, 1 g of fat and 150 mg of sodium, plus 15.5 g of EAAs. Free-form BCAAs are added, but the label does not give amounts. A creamer (sunflower oil, maltodextrin, modified food starch) and guar gum are in the mix, and it is sweetened with sucralose and acesulfame potassium. It contains milk and soy. Informed Choice is per the retailer listing; the registry could not be reached, so we have not confirmed it. At the dated price on file ($119.99 for 40 servings at Vitacost, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $2.50 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is cost. Myprotein Clear Whey Isolate, also a hydrolyzed whey, scores 76 at $1.69 per 25 g. Dymatize ISO100 Hydrolyzed scores 64 at $2.77. Hydrowhey costs about the same as ISO100 and gives you 30 g per scoop.
optimum-nutrition-platinum-hydrowhey.bestFor: Buyers set on hydrolyzed whey isolate with 30 g per scoop
optimum-nutrition-platinum-hydrowhey.skipIf: You want a cheaper isolate or avoid sucralose and creamers

verdict: Optimum Nutrition Serious Mass is a high-calorie weight gainer, and worth buying only if you struggle to eat enough and want sweetened shakes. If you have diabetes or other health conditions, talk with a doctor or dietitian before adding 1,260 calories a day. It scores 13 and ranks 99 of 100.

Two scoops (340 g) of Vanilla give you 50 g of protein, so protein is only 15% of the serving, at about 25 calories per gram of protein. Maltodextrin leads the label, with 253 g of carbs, 30 g of sugars (8 g added), 680 mg of sodium and 5 g of creatine monohydrate. It is sweetened with acesulfame potassium and sucralose and declares milk and soy. It is not on the NSF Certified for Sport list, and an Informed Choice entry labeled ASPAC is not confirmed for the US product. At the dated price on file ($57.88 for 8 servings on Amazon, checked 2026-11-19), it costs $3.62 per 25 g of protein. ON's own site listed $74.49 the same day.

The trade-off is sweeteners for convenience. Naked Mass, another milk-protein gainer, costs about the same per 25 g of protein ($3.64) with no sweeteners in its unflavored version, while Serious Mass adds creatine and flavors.
optimum-nutrition-serious-mass.bestFor: Hard gainers who want a flavored gainer with added creatine
optimum-nutrition-serious-mass.skipIf: You want a protein powder, avoid artificial sweeteners or need certification

verdict: Orgain Organic Plant Protein is widely available and organic, but its label is less than half protein, and we cannot give a cost per serving from the price on file. It scores 21 and ranks 97 of 100.

Two scoops (46 g) of Creamy Chocolate Fudge give you 21 g of protein, so protein is 46% of the serving, at about 7.1 calories per gram of protein. The protein is organic pea, brown rice, mung bean and chia. A creamer base, agave inulin, acacia, guar and xanthan gum bring 15 g of carbs and 7 g of fiber, and sodium is 390 mg. It is sweetened with stevia (Reb A). The panel we used did not show a total sugars figure, and retailers note that sweeteners vary across package versions, some listing erythritol, so read your tub. USDA Organic and Kosher are per Orgain. The brand listed a 2.03 lb canister at $37.99 on 2026-11-01 without a servings count, so there is no cost per 25 g at the dated price on file.
The trade-off is density. Garden of Life Raw Organic Protein, also an organic plant blend, is 67% protein at $2.03 per 25 g, so you get far more protein per scoop.
orgain-organic-plant-protein.bestFor: Shoppers who want an easy-to-find organic plant protein
orgain-organic-plant-protein.skipIf: You want a dense scoop, fewer gums or a known cost per serving

verdict: OWYN Pro Elite is a good value plant protein if you need a label free of the major allergens. It is cheap per gram of protein for a vegan powder, but the two-scoop serving is bulky, and its sodium is high.

The label maths for Chocolate: 30 g of protein in a two-scoop 49.8 g serving is 60% protein, and 180 calories works out to 6.0 calories per gram of protein. Carbs are 5 g, sugar 0 g, fat 4 g, fiber 3 g and sodium 440 mg. Protein comes from pea and pumpkin, topped up with an added amino acid blend that includes leucine, isoleucine and valine. The serving also adds a vitamin blend, a Bacillus coagulans probiotic and a greens blend. It is sweetened with monk fruit extract and uses organic guar gum. No allergens are declared; OWYN says it is free of dairy, soy, peanuts, tree nuts, sesame and gluten. Kosher is a claim per OWYN, and we could not check the Informed registry. At the dated price on file ($49.99 for 27 servings on the brand site, checked 2026-11-01) you pay about $1.54 per 25 g. Label Score 48, rank 71 of 100.

The trade-off is protein share for allergen coverage. Garden of Life Sport Organic Plant-Based Protein gives the same 30 g at 68% protein with a confirmed NSF Certified for Sport listing, but costs about $1.84 per 25 g.
owyn-plant-protein-powder.bestFor: Allergy-conscious buyers who want an affordable vegan protein
owyn-plant-protein-powder.skipIf: You watch sodium or want a compact single scoop

verdict: Paleovalley 100% Grass Fed Bone Broth Protein is worth it only if you specifically want a single-ingredient bone broth powder. As a muscle-building protein it is expensive and low in leucine, so most lifters will get more from a whey or a cheaper bone broth.

The label maths for Unflavored: 15 g of protein in a 17 g scoop is 88% protein, and 70 calories works out to about 4.7 calories per gram of protein. Sodium is 100 mg; carbs, sugar and fat are not printed on the panel. The only ingredient is beef bone broth powder, so there are no sweeteners, gums or flagged additives in this flavor. Flavored versions add coconut milk powder and monk fruit. Paleovalley's published amino profile shows 0.58 g leucine and about 1.26 g BCAAs per scoop. We found no registry certification; Paleovalley says it does third-party pesticide testing. At the dated price on file ($59.99 for a 30-serving bag on the brand site, checked 2026-11-01) you pay about $3.33 per 25 g, one of the highest in our animal-protein group. Label Score 51, rank 61 of 100.

The trade-off is cost per gram. Ancient Nutrition Bone Broth Protein gives 20 g per serving at 90% protein for about $2.39 per 25 g and scores 60, so it is the better value if you want bone broth protein but do not need Paleovalley's one-ingredient label.
paleovalley-bone-broth-protein.bestFor: Buyers who want an unflavored single-ingredient bone broth powder
paleovalley-bone-broth-protein.skipIf: Your goal is muscle gain or the lowest cost per gram

verdict: PB2 Performance Peanut Protein is a cheap, simple-label option if you want a peanut-based plant powder, but it is closer to a protein-rich food than a lean protein isolate. It scores 32 and ranks 89 of 100.

Two scoops (45 g) of Dutch Cocoa give you 20 g of protein, so protein is 44% of the serving, at 9.5 calories per gram of protein. That is because roasted peanuts lead the label, bringing 17 g of carbs, 8 g of fiber (partly from inulin) and 5 g of fat. Brown rice protein, cocoa, salt and monk fruit complete a six-ingredient list with no flagged additives. It contains peanuts. Non-GMO Project, Certified Gluten-Free and Kosher are per PB2; we have not confirmed them in a registry. At the dated price on file ($26.99 for about 20 servings, checked 2026-11-19), it costs $1.69 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is density. Naked Pea, also in the plant family, is 90% protein at $0.71 per 25 g, so it delivers more protein for fewer calories and less money. Choose PB2 if you want the peanut base and fiber.
pb2-performance-peanut-protein.bestFor: Buyers who want a short-label, peanut-based plant powder on a budget
pb2-performance-peanut-protein.skipIf: You have a peanut allergy or want a lean, high-protein scoop

verdict: PEScience Select Protein is a decent choice if you want a blend of casein and whey proteins with a long flavor list. On price and certification, though, it is not a standout.

The label maths for Gourmet Vanilla: 24 g of protein in a 31 g scoop is 77% protein, and 120 calories works out to 5.0 calories per gram of protein. Carbs are 2.5 g, sugar 1.5 g, fat 1.5 g and sodium 230 mg, with about 5 g BCAAs stated on the label. The protein comes from milk protein isolate, whey protein concentrate and leucine peptides. It is sweetened with sucralose and acesulfame potassium and uses guar gum. The label says it contains milk and soy, though no soy ingredient is named. Panels differ by flavor; Chocolate Peanut Butter Cup lists 23 g of protein. We did not find it in the NSF or Informed registries; 'third-party lab tested' is a PEScience claim. At the dated price on file ($54.99 for 27 servings at Vitacost, checked 2026-11-01) you pay about $2.12 per 25 g. Label Score 54, rank 54 of 100.

The trade-off is cost. Quest Nutrition Protein Powder, another milk protein blend, puts protein at 73% of the scoop for about $1.41 per 25 g and scores 58, so it is the cheaper blend if price matters more than flavor choice.
pescience-select-protein.bestFor: Shoppers who want a whey-casein blend with many flavors
pescience-select-protein.skipIf: You avoid artificial sweeteners or want a certified tub

verdict: Premier Protein 100% Whey is a good value if you want a lot of protein per serving from a grocery-store brand and don't mind artificial sweeteners. It scores 60 on our Label Score, rank 36 of 100.

The Chocolate Milkshake label lists 30 g of protein in a 41 g, two-scoop serving, so 73% of the serving is protein, at 150 calories, or 5.0 calories per gram of protein. It has 3 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar, 2 g of fat and 170 mg of sodium. The protein is a blend of whey isolate and concentrate. Under 2% of the formula are soluble corn fiber, sunflower lecithin, natural and artificial flavors, acesulfame potassium, sucralose, xanthan gum and salt. The gluten-free and kosher marks are per the retailer, with no certifier named, so no certification is on file. At the dated price on file ($29.99 for 17 servings at Target, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $1.47 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is certification. Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey, another whey blend, scores 78 at $1.44 per 25 g and has NSF Certified for Sport confirmed in the registry. For about the same cost you get a verified tub. Premier's tub is also small, so you'll be restocking every 17 servings.
premier-protein-powder.bestFor: Shoppers who want 30 g of whey per serving from a grocery brand
premier-protein-powder.skipIf: You avoid sucralose or need a certified product

verdict: ProDough Gourmet Whey Protein Powder is worth it if you want bakery-style flavors in a whey isolate with no artificial sweeteners. It is expensive per gram of protein, and the brand's product page showed it sold out, with pre-orders only, on the date of our price check.

The label maths for Vanilla Bean: 25 g of protein in a 33.5 g scoop is 75% protein, and 117 calories works out to about 4.7 calories per gram of protein. Carbs are 2 g, sugar 1 g, fat 1 g and sodium 250 mg. The protein is whey isolate plus non-fat milk powder, with cocoa butter powder, guar gum and a digestive enzyme blend. It is sweetened with glucosylated stevia extract and fermented Reb M. Milk is the allergen, and the label's facility statement also lists nuts, peanuts, wheat, soy and eggs. We found no third-party certification. At the dated price on file ($59.99 for a 20-serving bag on the brand site, checked 2026-11-01) you pay about $3.00 per 25 g. Other flavors run 117 to 128 calories and 25 to 26 g of protein. Label Score 49, rank 66 of 100.

The trade-off is cost. Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate gives 28 g per serving at 80% protein for about $1.93 per 25 g and scores 77, so it is the better value if flavor variety is not your priority.
prodough-protein-powder.bestFor: Buyers who want dessert flavors without artificial sweeteners
prodough-protein-powder.skipIf: You want a lower cost per gram or a product in stock

verdict: Promix Grass-Fed Whey Protein Powder is worth buying if you want an unsweetened grass-fed whey with a short label and no gums. It scores 70 on our Label Score and ranks 16th overall.

The ingredients are grass-fed whey concentrate and sunflower lecithin. A 31 g serving (two scoops) gives 25 g of protein, about 81 percent of the scoop, at 120 calories, or 4.8 calories per gram of protein, with 3 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar, 1.5 g of fat and 120 mg of sodium. There are no sweeteners or flagged additives. Promix publishes 3.0 g of leucine and 5.9 g of BCAAs. It has no certification on our list: Promix says it tests with Eurofins, and it is not in the NSF Certified for Sport registry. At the dated price on file, $64 for the 2.5 lb bag on the brand site, it costs about $1.73 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is the lack of a sport certification. Naked Whey is a near-identical plain grass-fed concentrate with an NSF Contents badge per Naked Nutrition, at about $1.84 per 25 g. Promix also sells a separate whey isolate, which is not this product.
promix-whey-protein.bestFor: Buyers who want an unsweetened grass-fed whey with no gums

verdict: Puori PW1 is worth buying if you want the shortest possible label and will pay for it. It is a single-ingredient grass-fed whey concentrate, and it earns a Label Score of 64, rank 26 of 100. If price per gram matters more than purity of the ingredient list, there are better buys.

The unflavored label gives you 24 g of protein in a 30 g scoop, so 80% of the scoop is protein, at 120 calories, or 5.0 calories per gram of protein. The only ingredient is whey protein concentrate: no sweeteners, no gums, no flavors. Puori also publishes 2.7 g of leucine and 6 g of BCAAs per serving. The Clean Label Project certification is per Puori; we have not confirmed it in a registry, and no heavy-metal figures are on file. At the dated price on file ($79 for 30 servings, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $2.74 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is cost. Naked Whey, another whey concentrate in our whey family, scores 74 at $1.84 per 25 g, and Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey, with NSF Certified for Sport confirmed in the registry, scores 78 at $1.44. You pay roughly a dollar extra per 25 g of protein for Puori's grass-fed sourcing and batch-testing promise.
puori-pw1-whey.bestFor: Buyers who want a one-ingredient grass-fed whey and will pay extra
puori-pw1-whey.skipIf: You want the lowest cost per gram or a registry-verified certification

verdict: Pure Protein 100% Whey is an acceptable budget-aisle whey, but cheaper store-brand blends beat it on both protein density and price. It scores 37 and ranks 87 of 100.

The Vanilla Milkshake scoop is 39.6 g with 25 g of protein, so protein is 63% of the scoop, at 6.4 calories per gram of protein. The protein is whey concentrate and isolate, followed by maltodextrin, which helps explain the 9 g of carbs listed (the retailer panel is worth checking against the tub). It is sweetened with acesulfame potassium and sucralose, uses cellulose and xanthan gum, and declares milk and soy. It carries no third-party certification and Pure Protein claims none. At the dated price on file ($45.99 for 20 servings at Target via iHerb, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $2.30 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is filler. Equate Whey Protein Powder, also a whey blend, is 77% protein at $0.94 per 25 g, and Premier Protein is 73% at $1.47. Pure Protein suits you only if it is the tub on your local shelf.
pure-protein-whey.bestFor: Shoppers who want a familiar grocery-store whey
pure-protein-whey.skipIf: You want less maltodextrin or a lower cost per gram of protein

verdict: Quest Protein Powder is a good-value blend of whey isolate and casein if you're fine with sucralose and a few gums. It scores 58 on our Label Score, rank 44 of 100, and its cost per gram is among the lower ones for a branded powder.

The Chocolate Milkshake label lists 22 g of protein in a 30 g scoop, so 73% of the scoop is protein, at 110 calories, or 5.0 calories per gram of protein. It has 3 g of carbs, under 1 g of sugar (0 g added), 0.5 g of fat, 1 g of fiber and 120 mg of sodium. The protein comes from whey isolate, micellar casein and milk protein isolate. It is sweetened with sucralose and stevia and thickened with cellulose gum and xanthan gum. It contains milk and may contain soy lecithin. The gluten-free and kosher marks don't name a certifier, so no certification is on file, and it is not on the NSF Certified for Sport list. At the dated price on file ($55.99 for about 45 servings, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $1.41 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is a smaller scoop and no certification. Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey costs about the same at $1.44 per 25 g and scores 78, with NSF Certified for Sport confirmed. Pick Quest if you want micellar casein in the mix.
quest-protein-powder.bestFor: Budget buyers who want whey and casein in one scoop
quest-protein-powder.skipIf: You avoid sucralose and gums or need a certified tub

verdict: RAW Nutrition BUM Itholate (formerly CBUM Itholate) is a premium-priced isolate built around mix-ins, and you pay for flavor rather than label quality. It scores 34 and ranks 88 of 100.

The Milk and Cookies scoop is 36 g with 25 g of protein, so protein is 69% of the scoop, at 5.6 calories per gram of protein. The base is whey isolate, but this flavor adds MCT oil powder, chocolate cookie pieces and mini marshmallows, which bring sugar and corn syrup (3 g total sugars), plus guar gum, gum acacia and xanthan gum. It is sweetened with sucralose and acesulfame potassium and declares milk and soy. The brand page shows an Informed Protein badge, a program outside our certification list, and the product is not on the NSF list. The page also carries a Prop 65 lead warning. At the dated price on file ($79.99 for 25 servings, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $3.20 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is price for mix-ins. Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey Isolate, also a whey isolate, is 80% protein at $1.93 per 25 g with a far shorter label. Macros vary by flavor, so check your flavor's panel.
raw-nutrition-cbum-itholate.bestFor: Chris Bumstead fans who want a dessert-style isolate
raw-nutrition-cbum-itholate.skipIf: You want a plain isolate or a lower cost per gram of protein

verdict: Redcon1 MRE Lite is a reasonable buy if you want a whey-free animal protein blend at a mainstream price and don't mind artificial sweeteners. It scores 64 on our Label Score, rank 27 of 100, and is one of the cheaper options in our animal-protein family.

The current Vanilla Milkshake label lists 26 g of protein in a 31.5 g scoop, so 83% of the scoop is protein, at 120 calories, or 4.6 calories per gram of protein. The blend leads with beef collagen peptides, then pea, brown rice, chicken, egg albumen and salmon protein, plus milk protein concentrate. It is not whey, but it does contain milk, egg and fish. It is sweetened with sucralose and acesulfame potassium and uses sodium carboxymethylcellulose as a thickener. No certification is listed, and it was not found on the NSF Certified for Sport list. At the dated price on file ($46.99 for 30 servings, checked 2026-11-19), it costs $1.51 per 25 g of protein.

The trade-off is the long blend: collagen peptides lead it, and no amino acid profile is published, so you can't see the leucine or BCAA content. Be Well by Kelly Grass-Fed Beef Protein scores 67 at $2.35 per 25 g. You save money with MRE Lite, but you get more sweeteners and additives. Redcon1 also reformulated this year, so check that your tub matches the 26 g label.
redcon1-mre-lite.bestFor: Lifters who want a whey-free animal blend at a low cost per gram
redcon1-mre-lite.skipIf: You avoid artificial sweeteners, or you need dairy-, egg- or fish-free

verdict: Ritual Essential Protein 18+ makes sense only if you value its traceability and published lot tests enough to pay one of the highest prices per gram of pea protein we track. It scores 42 and ranks 79 of 100.

A 31 g serving (5 tablespoons, not a scoop) gives you 20 g of organic pea protein, so protein is 65% of the serving, at 6 calories per gram of protein. Ritual adds 150 mg choline and 400 mg L-methionine. It is sweetened with Reb M and monk fruit, uses xanthan gum and MCT oil, and the brand says it is free of major allergens. NSF Contents Certified and the Clean Label Project award are per Ritual; we have not confirmed them in a registry. Ritual also publishes a lot test showing cadmium at 0.03 ppm and arsenic, lead and mercury below reporting limits. At the dated price on file ($50 for 15 servings, checked 2026-11-01, plus $10.99 shipping for non-members), it costs $4.17 per 25 g of protein.
The trade-off is cost. NOW Sports Pea Protein, also a pea protein, is 73% protein at $0.91 per 25 g. Ritual costs over four times as much for less protein per serving.
ritual-essential-protein-18.bestFor: Adults who want a pea shake with published heavy-metal lot results
ritual-essential-protein-18.skipIf: You are shopping on cost per gram of protein

verdict: RYSE Loaded Protein is for buyers who want licensed snack-brand flavors, such as Jet-Puffed Marshmallow and Skippy Peanut Butter, and are willing to accept a longer label for them. It scores 56 on our Label Score, rank 49 of 100.

The Jet-Puffed Marshmallow label lists 25 g of protein in a 33.9 g scoop, so 74% of the scoop is protein, at 130 calories, or 5.2 calories per gram of protein. It has 3 g of carbs, 1 g of sugar, 2.5 g of fat and 240 mg of sodium. The protein is instantized whey isolate and concentrate. MCT powder adds fat, and agave inulin adds fiber. The label also lists an unitemized gum blend, natural and artificial flavor, sucralose and acesulfame potassium. It contains milk and soy. No certification is on file, and it is not on the NSF Certified for Sport or Informed lists. At the dated price on file ($49.99 for 27 servings at Vitacost, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $1.85 per 25 g of protein. Panels vary a lot by flavor.

The trade-off is that you pay for flavor rather than for label quality. GHOST Whey, another flavor-led whey blend, scores 48 at $2.12 per 25 g, so RYSE is the cheaper of the two. Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey scores 78 at $1.44 if flavor novelty doesn't matter to you.
ryse-loaded-protein.bestFor: Buyers who want snack-brand flavors in a whey blend
ryse-loaded-protein.skipIf: You want a short label, a certification or no artificial sweeteners

verdict: SEEQ Clear Protein is a good pick if you want a juice-style clear whey without artificial sweeteners, but it costs more per gram than the leading clear wheys. It scores 56 on our Label Score, rank 50 of 100.

The Strawberry Lemonade label lists 22 g of protein in a 28 g scoop, so 79% of the scoop is protein, at 100 calories, or 4.5 calories per gram of protein. It has 1 g of carbs, no sugar, fat or fiber, and only 10 mg of sodium. SEEQ also claims 4.5 g of BCAAs. Besides the isolate, the label lists natural flavors, citric and malic acids, Reb M stevia, monk fruit, polysorbate 80, red beet powder for color and silicone antifoam. No certification is on file. At the dated price on file ($54 for 22 servings, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $2.79 per 25 g of protein. Older packs at Target list sucralose, so check the label on the tub you buy.

The trade-off is price. Myprotein Clear Whey Isolate scores 76 at $1.69 per 25 g, and Isopure Infusions, sweetened with stevia only, scores 63 at $2.31. You'd pay about 50 cents more per 25 g for SEEQ than for Isopure.
seeq-clear-whey-isolate.bestFor: Buyers who want a clear whey sweetened with stevia and monk fruit
seeq-clear-whey-isolate.skipIf: You want the cheapest clear whey or a certified product

verdict: Sunwarrior Warrior Blend is a decent organic pea and hemp option if you want a short, stevia-sweetened label, but a scoop delivers only 16 g of protein. It scores 41 and ranks 81 of 100.

The Chocolate scoop is 25 g with 16 g of protein, so protein is 64% of the scoop, at 5.6 calories per gram of protein. The protein blend is organic pea, hemp seed and goji berry, with MCT oil, guar gum and organic stevia. USDA Organic and Kosher are per Sunwarrior, from the retailer listing; we have not confirmed them in a registry. The brand notes its facility may handle peanuts or tree nuts, and the MCT oil is coconut-derived. At the dated price on file ($49.47 for 30 servings at Vitacost, checked 2026-11-01), it costs $2.58 per 25 g of protein.

sunwarrior-warrior-blend.bestFor: Vegans who want an organic pea and hemp blend with stevia

verdict: Swanson Senior Muscle Retention Protein is aimed at adults over 60, but its label is more of a fortified shake mix than a dense protein powder. If you are buying it for an older relative, talk with their doctor or a dietitian about protein needs first. It scores 24 and ranks 94 of 100.

Most of the protein is whey concentrate, with some pea protein and goat milk, plus an organic six-grain blend, soluble fiber and MCTs, giving 11 g of carbs and 3.5 g of fiber. It is sweetened with stevia (Reb A). It declares milk, goat milk, wheat and soy, so it is not gluten-free. Swanson claims no third-party certification. At the dated price on file ($34.79 for 10 servings, checked 2026-11-19, when the vanilla was marked sold out), it costs $3.48 per 25 g of protein.
The trade-off is cost per gram of protein. Naked Whey, another whey concentrate, is 83% protein at $1.84 per 25 g, and adding protein to an older adult's diet does not require a senior-branded tub.
swanson-senior-muscle-retention-protein.bestFor: Older adults who want a stevia-sweetened whey shake with grains and fiber
swanson-senior-muscle-retention-protein.skipIf: You need gluten-free, want lower cost per gram, or want a plain whey

verdict: Thorne Whey Protein Isolate is worth buying if a confirmed NSF Certified for Sport listing matters to you, for example if you are a tested athlete. If it does not, you pay a premium for a scoop with a lower protein share than most isolates.

The label maths for Chocolate: 21 g of protein in a 30.2 g scoop is 70% protein, and 100 calories works out to about 4.8 calories per gram of protein. Carbs are 4 g, sugar 2 g (including 1 g added), fat 1 g, fiber 1 g and sodium 105 mg, with 2.2 g leucine. It is sweetened with evaporated cane juice sugar and rebaudioside A from stevia and uses xanthan gum and carboxymethylcellulose gum, plus a bromelain and papain blend. The only allergen is milk. We confirmed NSF Certified for Sport in the nsfsport.com registry for both Chocolate and Vanilla. Thorne's brand page carries a Prop 65 lead warning. At the dated price on file ($65 for 30 scoops on the brand site, checked 2026-11-01) you pay about $2.58 per 25 g. Label Score 54, rank 55 of 100.

The trade-off is protein share for certification. Klean Athlete Klean Isolate, also confirmed NSF Certified for Sport, puts protein at 90% of the scoop but costs about $3.97 per 25 g, so Thorne is the cheaper certified isolate while Klean is the leaner one.
thorne-whey-protein-isolate.bestFor: Tested athletes who want a confirmed NSF Certified for Sport isolate
thorne-whey-protein-isolate.skipIf: You do not need certification and want more protein per dollar

verdict: Transparent Labs 100% Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate is worth it if you want a high-protein scoop with stevia instead of artificial sweeteners, and you accept a premium price. It scores 77 on our Label Score and ranks ninth overall.

transparent-labs-grass-fed-whey-isolate.bestFor: Buyers who want a big-protein whey isolate sweetened with stevia
transparent-labs-grass-fed-whey-isolate.skipIf: You want the cheapest whey per gram or a registry-verified certification

verdict: Truvani Organic Plant Based Protein is a strong choice if label simplicity comes first: six ingredients, monk fruit only, and no gums. The catch is that we have no current price, so we cannot judge value. It scores 41 and ranks 82 of 100.

verdict: Truvani Protein + Greens is a greens powder with some protein, not a protein powder you should buy for protein. At 10 g per scoop, it has the highest cost per 25 g of protein in our database. It scores 29 and ranks 91 of 100.

verdict: Vital Proteins Collagen Peptides is worth buying if you want an unflavored collagen to stir into coffee or food, not a complete protein for building muscle. It scores 74 on our Label Score and ranks 14th overall.
